title: Low 12-month rainfall-rank recovery gave no clear excess over reordered years in three British countries in 1901-2025
abstract: We tested recovery from low 12-month rainfall ranks in England, Wales and Scotland in 1901-2025. We used Met Office country rainfall. Recovery ran from the calendar-month 10th percentile to its median, with a 24-month cap. The equal-country mean was 13.79 months across 71 episodes. In 1,999 references, complete years were reordered within five 25-year periods, with countries kept together. The reference mean was 13.32 months and the central 95% reference range was 11.78 to 14.95 months. The upper-tail fraction was 0.271. This gives no clear excess under this reference. It does not prove independence or an absent physical memory. This study extends a US campaign result to a different region and tests shorter block references. It does not refute the US result. Three correlated country means, few episodes, revised gridded data, fitted thresholds and reference exchangeability limit inference. Recovery of a rainfall index does not measure recovery of water stores. The package contains original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and reproduction instructions. External source records and episode tables are excluded.

display.caption: Observed capped mean recovery and central 95% ranges from reordered records. Ranges describe the references, not confidence limits on observed recovery.

citations.reason: Its capped rank-recovery endpoint and US result motivate an independent geographic test. We use new code and a whole-year primary reference.
